page.layout: One page of running text in one column; no margin notes. Running head at the top above the text. Page number at the top left. Text ends at the bottom with a catchword-like word "juven-" (a line-end hyphenated word, treated as the last line).

main_text.p: Deinde etiam, quia nullum ex aliis animalium generibus invenitur, quod in speciebus suis, sive inter se collatis, sive per singulis, tantam exhibeat temperamentorum varietatem.
Si namque conferantur inter se corpora humana plura, unius ab altero discrepans deprehenditur temperamentum.

Quod evenit partim ratione virtutis feminis parentum, & influentiæ stellarum in conceptione: partim etiam ratione rerum externarum, quibus in quotidiana vita est opus, ut aeris in quo vivitur, victus, exercitiorum, &c.
Cujusq; autem hominis corpus seorsim si attendatur, illud etiam plures ætatis differentias, temperamentis discrepantes, fortitur.
Ætate enim affcendente, quæ primos 35. annos a nativitate completitur, homo viribus corporis crescens, & membra expeditiora, & spiritus ad obeundas actiones animæ aptiores subinde adipiscitur.
Quæ ætas ascendens, suis rursum gradibus constat, cum pueritia & adolescentia, tum juventute.

Pueritia completitur primos ætatis annos 15. Cujus prima pars, a nativitate ad tertium annum, est infantia: hinc Media pueritia usq; ad annum 12: Præceps inde pueritia & adolescentiæ vicina, usq; ad 15. annum.
Adolescentia est intermedia ætas ascendens, a 15. ætatis anno ad 25. usq; procurrens.

page.notes: Page 88 of the book, with the head "DE CORPORE HUMANO." The last word "juven-" is a line-end hyphen, which continues on the next page, so it is left as a hyphenated fragment. Doubtful readings: "per singulis" (the scan reads "per fe fingulis", which is probably "per se singulis" with the long s printed as f; I have kept the plain s and marked nothing, as the sense is clear). "Ætate enim affcendente" is printed as an italic word; the italic is shown as plain text here because the scan's italic is faint. "Cujusq; autem" and "seorsim si" are read with some uncertainty. "Quæ ætas ascendens" and "Pueritia completitur" were read with reasonable care. The line "Cujus prima pars... ad tertium annum" is read as printed. The numbers "35.", "15.", "12:", "25." are as printed on the scan.
